name: Jordan
label: Playlist organizer weighing Apple Music
who: I have moved between Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music over the years, and I keep coming back to Spotify for its search and multi-device sync. I care most about organizing my playlists and library, and I will pay for a small tool when it saves me from rebuilding everything by hand.
value_for_money: Says small third-party tools were worth it: about $2 to move playlists off Apple Music and roughly $5 one-time for listening history [8][22]. Stays on the Spotify subscription because rebuilding playlists elsewhere would be too much work [37]. Says choosing specific songs is a Premium feature [21], and was surprised a free account could play a chosen song directly [30].
loyalty: Stays for the search tools, interface and multi-device sync [33], and because moving years of playlists elsewhere is a big cost [37]. Has already left Apple Music once for storage reasons [4]. Says they would stop their subscription if a change they dislike happened [32].
pain_points: Cannot play one artist's songs without the whole discography
Cannot see the songs in a playlist, only recommended tracks
Reordering playlists on mobile is clumsy
No way to tag songs or albums
likes: Playlists from other users for discovery
reasons_to_stay: They value Spotify's search, interface and multi-device sync enough to keep returning after trying Apple Music [33]. They also keep the subscription because rebuilding years of playlists elsewhere would be too much work [37].
tone: Practical and friendly, asking how-to questions and sharing workarounds.
